page: Vultr vx1-g-32c-128g-1920s is a general-purpose cloud instance within the VX1 Cloud Compute family. It features 32 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 16 physical cores on an AMD EPYC x86_64 processor clocked at 2.0 GHz, supporting two threads per core. Memory capacity is configured at 128 GB of RAM, preserving a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 4 GB per virtual core. Local storage is fully integrated via a bundled 1920 GB NVMe SSD, and networking includes one complimentary public IPv4 address without discrete GPU acceleration.

Hardware benchmark metrics demonstrate high throughput across CPU and memory subsystems. The AMD processor features AVX-512 extensions including AVX-512 VNNI and BF16, which directly contribute to top-tier single-core stress-ng scores of 3691.88 and strong Geekbench multi-core performance of 15978.0. Uncached large-block memory read bandwidth reached 295.05 GB/s, while write operations achieved 194.79 GB/s, placing both in the upper performance tiers. Database operations benchmarked at 22459.47 operations per second, alongside Redis SET performance sustaining 63.95 million operations per second.

The bundled NVMe storage and balanced resource profile deliver strong qualitative cost efficiency for enterprise services requiring dedicated host resources without the overhead of external SAN latency. While multi-core compilation and sustained ray tracing test results settle in the middle tiers, compression benchmarks and static web serving throughput (75.47 GB/s) remain highly competitive. This instance is well configured for production relational databases, memory caching layers, container clusters, ETL pipelines, and high-concurrency web serving.
description: Vultr vx1-g-32c-128g-1920s is a balanced cloud compute instance featuring 32 dedicated vCPUs (16 physical cores) powered by an AMD EPYC x86_64 processor clocked at 2.0 GHz. It includes 128 GB of system memory, providing a consistent 1:4 CPU-to-memory ratio, and is bundled with a 1920 GB local NVMe SSD without discrete GPU hardware. Benchmark results indicate top-tier memory write bandwidth of 194.79 GB/s, strong uncached read bandwidth of 295.05 GB/s, and a PassMark memory score of 2989.46. With instruction set extensions including AVX-512 and cryptographic accelerators, this instance delivers strong results in Redis caching (63.95 million operations per second), static web serving throughput (75.47 GB/s), and database operations. It serves as a reliable platform for medium-to-large relational databases, distributed caching layers, ETL processing, and high-traffic production application backends.
